Wikipedia iOS app 8.0 on iOS 26

The Wikimedia Foundation’s iPhone app, version 8.0.0, whose floating glass tab bar and search button bend the photo that scrolls under them.

Source
Wikimedia Commons screenshot
Creator
Wikimedia Foundation
Made
2026 (release tag releases/8.0.0 dated April 13, 2026; screenshot April 19, 2026)
Style
Liquid Glass (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Liquid, calm, editorial
Evidence
Inspected the Commons screenshot IOS App 8.0.0 Explore.png (1179 × 2556) by EvanTech10, with a 1:1 crop of the tab bar. Also looked at the companion IOS App 8.0.0 Article.png. Not stored.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The app is open source under the MIT license. Its code calls Apple’s glassEffect API, for example in WMFHomeView.swift and WMFFindInPageView.swift. GitHub: wikimedia/wikipedia-ios.

Apple Developer: standard SwiftUI, UIKit, and AppKit controls and navigation elements “pick up the appearance and behavior of this material automatically”. Apple Developer: Liquid Glass.

Observed

  • Dark mode. A “Today” feed with a serif featured-article card and a “Picture of the day” photo of a green and violet faceted glass dome.
  • At the top, the Wikipedia “W” sits in a separate dark glass circle on the left, and two icons share a dark glass capsule on the right. Neither is pinned to the screen edge.
  • At the bottom, a glass capsule holds four tabs (Explore, Places, Saved, Activity), and a separate glass circle holds the search icon. Both float over the photo.
  • In the 1:1 crop the straight frame lines of the dome curve into loops just inside the rims of the capsule and the circle, while the middle stays nearly undistorted. A thin bright line marks the rim. The selected tab sits in a lighter inner capsule.
  • The Article screenshot shows the same pattern: a back button, a “W” circle, and a three-icon capsule float over the lead image, and a toolbar capsule floats over the article text.

Why it belongs

Because the app uses system components, it shows the default behavior of the material that any developer gets, not an Apple marketing render.

Borrow

Split navigation into a tab capsule and a separate search circle, so the most used action has its own target.
